content_units: Given your priorities—  career growth (40%)  ,   work-life balance (30%)  ,   cash compensation (20%)  , and   flexibility (10%)  —  Offer B in Madrid   comes out slightly ahead overall for a 3-year horizon, mainly because it is   better aligned to growth + lifestyle together  .
Context note: I used your stated living-cost assumptions and treated bonus as target cash, not guaranteed cash.
Factor   Weight   Offer A: Senior Data Analyst, Berlin   Offer B: Analytics Manager, Madrid

Career growth   40%     7.5/10   — strong brand potential; likely promotion in 24 months; but starts one level below manager     8.5/10   — higher title now; management scope earlier; smaller-company risk but faster leadership exposure

Work-life balance   30%     7.0/10   — 30 vacation days is strong; hybrid is reasonable; 25 min each way commute reduces time     8.5/10   — fully remote; lower day-to-day friction; 25 vacation days but better overall autonomy
Cash compensation   20%     8.8/10   — €78k + 10% bonus + 3% pension match; stronger total package     7.4/10   — €62k + 15% bonus; no pension match; lower absolute pay but lower living costs help
Flexibility   10%     7.0/10   — hybrid 2 days/week in office     9.5/10   — fully remote
-   Estimated annual surplus after living costs:
-   3-year gross target comp incl. pension match:   about   €264,420
- slower title progression at the start
- commute and office cadence reduce lifestyle upside
-   Estimated annual surplus after living costs:
-   3-year gross target comp incl. training budget:   about   €219,900
- lower cost base with remote work
- smaller-company title can be less portable than a stronger brand name
Recommendation: Choose Offer B (Madrid) if your stated priorities are exactly as given.
- Your highest priority is   career growth (40%)  , and B gives you a   manager title now  , which can materially improve your trajectory over 3 years.
- Your second priority is   work-life balance (30%)  , and   fully remote + lower living-cost pressure + no commute   is a meaningful advantage.
- Offer A clearly wins on   cash compensation  , but cash is only   20%   of your weighting, so it does not fully offset B’s edge in growth and lifestyle.
Why Offer A could still be the better choice
- If you value   financial upside more than your current weighting suggests  , A becomes very compelling.
- Over 3 years, A has roughly   €44.5k   more total package value on a target basis than B when including bonus, and about   €14.1k   more surplus versus your stated living costs.
- If the Berlin employer has a stronger reputation, that may narrow or even erase B’s title advantage in future hiring markets.
Why Offer B remains the better weighted fit
- A manager title now can compound faster than waiting 24 months for a promotion.
- Remote work creates weekly time savings and lower friction that materially supports sustainability over 3 years.
- The training budget adds a small but real career-capital benefit.
If you want the shortest answer:
-   Choose Offer B   if you want the role that best matches your   stated priorities  .
-   Choose Offer A   if you want to optimize for   money, package strength, and lower execution risk  .
